Maintenance Report — MNT-0031-005

Asset: WELL-0031 (SW-23 Well 031, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 30 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 30 Jun 2023 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 14 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0031-0036 on 2023-06-29 Report written: 02 Jul 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0031-0036 at 11:00 on 2023-06-29 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.3% of the pad area, estimated 3.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 238 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 190 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0031-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.48% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0031-0066 showed the wellhead at 9.5 °C with the air at 10.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0031-017

Asset: WELL-0031 (SW-23 Well 031, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 24 Jan 2025 08:00 · Finished: 12 Feb 2025 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 455 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0031-0115 on 2025-01-23 Report written: 12 Feb 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0031-0115 showed the wellhead at 4.4 °C with the air at 4.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0031-017 (WS-06).
